'''Kristin Schirmer''' (born 1967) is a German cell biologist and toxicologist. She is the Head of Department of Environmental Toxicology at the [[Swiss Federal Institute of Aquatic Science and Technology]] (Eawag)] and also a professor at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne]] ([[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]]) and [[ETH Zurich]]. Schirmer specializes in Molecular and Cellular Mechanisms of [[Toxicity]], [[Aquatic organism|Aquatic Organisms]], [[Chemical hazard|Chemical Hazard]] Assessment, [[Adverse outcome pathway|Adverse Outcome Pathways]], [[In vitro toxicology|in vitro]] Alternatives to Animal Testing, Fish Cell Lines and [[Biomonitoring]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=EPFL Online People Directory - Kristin Schirmer|url=https://people.epfl.ch/kristin.schirmer|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=18 new professors appointed at ETH Zurich and EPFL {{!}} ETH-Board|url=https://www.ethrat.ch/en/media/releases/appointments-dec20|access-date=2021-02-19|website=www.ethrat.ch|archive-date=2021-12-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211212231025/https://www.ethrat.ch/en/media/releases/appointments-dec20|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
From 1989 to 1994 Schirmer earned her biology diploma at the [[University of Hohenheim]] and the [[Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg|Martin-Luther-University Halle-Wittenberg.]] After that she continued as a Ph.D. student at the Department of Biology of the [[University of Waterloo]] in Canada, where she worked on her doctoral thesis on the development of [[in vitro]] toxicity assays with [[rainbow trout]] cells. From 1997 to 2001 Schirmer completed her Postdoctoral Training at the [[Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research]] and [[University of Waterloo]]. From 2001 to 2003 she was the Junior Research Group Leader at [[Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research|UFZ]] in Leipzig.<ref name=":0" />

== Career and research ==
In 2008 Kristin Schirmer was appointed as the new head of the Environmental Toxicology department at [[Swiss Federal Institute of Aquatic Science and Technology|Eawag]]. Before that she had already taught [[Ecotoxicology]] as a professor at the [[ETH Zurich]]. In 2011 Schirmer began teaching at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] and was awarded the title of adjunct professor.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

In 2019 the Swiss 3R Competence Centre, a nonprofit association located in [[Bern]], which promotes research for the replacement and reduction of animal experimentation,<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=The Swiss 3R Competence Centre|url=https://www.swiss3rcc.org/en/about-us|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214132703/https://www.swiss3rcc.org/en/about-us|archive-date=2021-12-14|access-date=|website=|url-status=dead}}</ref> awarded Kristin Schirmer and her colleague Melanie Fisher for their exceeding research work. They received [[International Organization for Standardization|ISO certification]] for a toxicity test utilizing cultured fish gill cells instead of fish, which proves to be a milestone in the promotion of alternate procedures to animal testing .<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Swiss 3RCC's 2019 3Rs Award|url=https://www.swiss3rcc.org/en/funding-awards/awards-prizes/2018|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref>

With other researchers from [[Swiss Federal Institute of Aquatic Science and Technology|Eawag]] Schirmer took part in developing a business idea named "Rainbow Biosystem", creating a fish-cell-based [[biosensor]] that provides a solution for managing and monitoring the quality of water. For this they received the 3rd prize in the business plan category by Venture, a Swiss start-up competition.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Venture|url=https://www.venture.ch/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=20 June 2017|title=Water monitoring with fish-cell-based biosensor awarded by Venture|url=https://www.hevs.ch/en/hes-so-valais-wallis/news/water-monitoring-with-fish-cell-based-biosensor-awarded-by-venture-15848|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref>

In December 2020 [[ETH Zurich]] appointed her as titular professor.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=11 December 2020|title=Kristin Schirmer becomes titular professor at the ETH Zurich|url=https://www.myscience.ch/news/wire/kristin_schirmer_becomes_titular_professor_at_the_eth_zurich-2020-eawag|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref>

Currently the main focus of her research is on the freshwater environment and on fish or single-cell organisms as experimental models, as well as on human-made products and chemicals, naturally occurring elements, biologically derived [[toxin]]s as stressors.<ref name=":0" />

== Awards and honors ==
Awards won include:<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Eawag - Swiss Federal Institute of Aquatic Science and Technology|url=https://www.eawag.ch/en/aboutus/portrait/organisation/staff/profile/kristin-schirmer/show/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref>
* 2019 Recipient of the 3RCC Award of the Swiss3R Competence Centre (together with her colleague Melanie Fischer)
* 2017 Venture competition – New business idea: the Rainbow Biosystem; 3rd prize
* 2007 SETAC Environmental Education Award
* 2007 Felix-Wankel Animal Welfare Research Award
* 2007 Technology Transfer Award for Ceramic Toximeter passives sampler (Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research - UFZ)
* 1998 W.B. Pearson Medal for recognition of creative research in a Doctoral thesis
* 1997 Best Student Platform Presentation Award, 24th Aquatic Toxicity Workshop
* 1994 - 1996 University of Waterloo and Ontario International Graduate Student Scholarship
